problem: How does lanthanide identity affect the coordination and conformational preferences of [Ln-KHQ]+ in water for Ln = La, Tb and Lu, and how firmly can those preferences be established?
facts: La and Lu solution NMR indicate chemically equivalent pendant arms under their reported complex-forming conditions; this does not uniquely assign a conformation.
Source La NMR was measured in D2O at pD6.5; Lu complex formation depended on pD, with full conversion reported by pD9.
Optional numerical ECP/basis resources are supplied with source hashes. A 4f-in-core pseudosinglet describes its explicit-electron model and does not assert physical Tb spin zero.
scope: Use the complete KHQ dianion C32H38N4O6(2−) and one La(III), Tb(III) or Lu(III), yielding [Ln-KHQ]+. Investigate aqueous coordination under a declared temperature and standard state; source thermodynamic context is 298 K. Distinguish this +1 species from the protonated +2 crystalline [La-HKHQ]2+ and from hydrolyzed species. Any added or removed water/proton must be accounted for chemically.
resource_facts: The platform supplies registered chemistry actions, native-software execution and selected Python runtimes. Inspect their actual capabilities and allocated resources. No specialist interface, license, cost or total compute budget is guaranteed by this task.
known_input_limits: No calibrated universal Ln solvent cavity radius or aqueous reference free energy is supplied. Model-dependent uncertainty in solvation and low-frequency entropy remains to be established by the chosen study.
